title: Constructivism Landscapes
subtitle: Landscapes made while I was reading about Constructivism — and learning to see structure in nature.

tiles: Studying the Constructivist way of looking
Mountains and water read as geometry
The pieces I wanted to keep
challenge: Constructivism taught me to look for the underlying structure of a scene — the axes, the planes, the rhythm. I wanted to see if I could hold onto that way of looking while working with something as unruly as a landscape.
approach: I read into the movement, then drafted many versions of mountain and water scenes, watching for the ones where the geometry and the natural form stopped fighting each other. I kept the six that taught me something and that I personally enjoyed.
result: A small set of landscapes that feel calm and a little formal in a way I like. They're available as prints for anyone else who enjoys seeing nature through that kind of structured eye.
